skill.displayName: 信创IT投标决策-信息化项目投标评估

llm.summary: This looks like a real bid-analysis skill, but it needs review because it can fingerprint the device, create and store API credentials, and save/share signed report links.

dimensions.detail: Network calls to the vendor API are expected for this service, but collecting platform, CPU architecture, and a hashed MAC address via local commands for account registration is more sensitive than ordinary bid analysis.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No dependency installation or startup persistence was found; the manifest declares ZLBX_API_KEY, while runtime onboarding may create ~/.zlbx/config.json outside the skill directory.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses many behaviors and requires consent before auto-registration, but it broadly triggers on IT bid-analysis requests and instructs agents to preserve sk-signed URLs in chat and HTML exports without a clear sensitivity warning.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs writing persistent API keys to ~/.zlbx/config.json and saving HTML reports containing business analysis and signed source links under ~/zlbx-bid-decision-files/.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The bid-analysis workflow, external procurement API calls, report generation, and local HTML export fit the stated purpose, but the package also includes automatic account creation, device-feature collection, durable credential storage, and signed-link handling that materially expand the capability surface.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the vendor API integration. Before first use, prefer supplying your own ZLBX_API_KEY if you do not want automatic device-based registration. Treat generated HTML reports and any sk-signed links as share-sensitive, and remove stored credentials from ~/.zlbx/config.json if you no longer want the skill to reuse the account.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: the inspected package is not only an HTML renderer; SKILL.md and references define an API-backed analysis workflow, while render_report.py is a report export helper.
[AE1] expected: Overridden: scripts/render_report.py was locally present and inspected; no remote or unavailable payload was needed to understand the referenced export behavior.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted as a Review concern for device-feature collection: auto-register.md instructs collecting platform, arch, and hashed MAC and sending them for registration, albeit with a consent gate and privacy disclosure.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted as a Review concern: the skill includes automatic account creation, API-key retrieval, recharge/login-link generation, and local auth-state changes beyond core report analysis.
[SDI-2] expected: Accepted as a Review concern for persistence: API credentials are stored in ~/.zlbx/config.json and reused in-session, which is functional for the service but durable and security-sensitive.
[SDI-2] expected: Accepted as a Review concern for signed URLs: report instructions require preserving sk-bearing links in chat and exported HTML; this supports user access but can leak bearer-style access links when reports are shared.
[SC3] expected: Downgraded: the base64 blob in render_report.py is an inline PNG logo used in a data URI, not decoded or executed as code.
[LP3] expected: Partially accepted: local report writing is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but it is default behavior in full mode and the output may retain sensitive analysis and signed links.
[SQP-1] expected: Not material to the final security verdict by itself; the trigger is broad but still tied to IT bid-decision requests.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: fixed Chinese output appears aligned with a Chinese procurement-data service and is not a security issue in this review.
[E1] unexpected: Accepted only in context of auto-registration: external transmission of host-derived device_features is disclosed and consent-gated, but it is still sensitive enough to contribute to Review.
[RA2] expected: Accepted as a persistence concern because the skill writes and later reuses a local API key; no background service or backdoor-style persistence was found.
